passes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one exploratory creature concept illustration for Arkya, a stylized painted 3D fantasy MMORPG. This is a visual proposal, not a game-ready mesh.
Primary request: design the original forest monster "Brise-Sève" as a grounded, memorable, dangerous territorial beast.
Subject: ONE muscular quadruped combining the weight and low center of gravity of a boar with the broad planted forepaws and shoulder power of a badger-bear. About 1.45 meters at the shoulders, 2.3 meters long as a proposed scale. Broad wedge-shaped head, short thick muzzle, small alert ears, deep-set amber eyes beneath a sculpted brow. Its identifying feature is a natural bark face shield shaped into three broad interlocking plates, ending in TWO thick pale root-tusks that curve outwards and upward. Tusks must remain distinct from the face silhouette. The body has living dark chestnut hide, warm ochre-brown bark armor only on the face, shoulders and ridge of the back, and a sweeping jade-green moss mane modeled in a few large sculpted locks. Strong high shoulders, lower hips, short tufted tail, exactly four anatomically coherent stout legs, thick broad paws with simple blunt rootlike claws. The near front foot is planted forward. Sparse amber resin glows in just a few cracks at the base of the two tusks, with no bloom washing out their edges. No tree growing on its back. Threatening but expressive and suitable for a welcoming fantasy world.
Composition/framing: landscape 1536x1024, one complete creature in a strong front three-quarter view facing left, camera near upper body height slightly looking down so the back armor is visible. Full body, all feet, both tusks and tail comfortably within frame. Creature occupies 75 percent of the picture width. Its weight rests convincingly on a pale earthen forest trail with small stones and a contact shadow. The head and tusks are the focal point. Enough negative space around silhouette.
Style/medium: a polished game creature concept that looks like an expertly sculpted and hand-painted 3D character. Continuous smooth modeled volumes, carefully chosen broad surface planes, softened bevels, painted tonal gradients following anatomy, broad stylized bark grain and deliberate color variation. The fur and moss consist of large solid tapered locks, never individual hairs. Strong silhouette and clear forms that survive a 160-pixel thumbnail. Refined craft and clean anatomical construction, no coarse low-poly faceting, no photorealism, no noisy microtexture.
Color palette: warm chestnut hide and ochre bark as the large middle-value mass, deep jade moss crest, pale ivory root tusks as the high-value focal shapes, very limited amber eye and resin accents. No neon green.
Scene/backdrop: understated painted woodland clearing, pale desaturated sage atmosphere, softly simplified trunks far behind and dark green foliage at the outer edges. Background must stay much simpler and lower contrast than the subject. Warm soft daylight from upper left, cool teal ambient shadows, restrained natural contact shadows. A calm forest context making the creature readable, not an epic battle scene.
Constraints: readable distinction between matte skin, ridged painted bark, solid sculpted moss and slightly glossy resin. Exactly one creature, no other characters, no tiny decorative clutter, no floating particles hiding its shape, no armor straps, no human costume, no weapons, no antlers, no oversized crystal, no gore. No writing, labels, watermarks, logos, sheet borders or UI.

Use case: style-transfer. Edit the provided forest beast concept. Keep the exact creature identity, quadruped anatomy, stance, four feet, pair of ivory root-tusks, broad bark-mask face, amber eyes, high shoulders, large moss crest, short tail, chestnut/ochre/green palette, three-quarter framing and forest clearing composition. Change ONLY the rendering and surface design complexity to match an actual stylized hand-painted MMORPG game character.
Decisively simplify all surfaces: turn the dozens of small facial bark splinters into THREE to FIVE big beautifully sculpted interlocking shield plates. Turn the moss mane into SIX to EIGHT large soft sculpted sweeping locks with painted gradients, no individual leaves. Hide/fur must read as smooth broad solid sculpted masses with only a few deliberate tuft contours at elbows and chest: zero individual hair strands. The shoulder/back bark is a handful of broad beveled plates. Remove 85 percent of all tiny grooves, scratches, shards, leaflets, stippling and photographic material noise. Preserve the primary silhouette and pose.
Render with continuous polished 3D model forms and rich painterly gradients following the anatomy, clean soft bevels, warm highlights and colored cool shadows. NOT faceted low poly, NOT realistic fur or bark scans, NOT cinematic photorealism. Think refined sculpted collectible/game asset hand-painted finish with simple material definition. Pale tusks have only two or three broad painted grain streaks. Amber resin stays very small, contained at tusk roots. Simplify the forest background into large soft painted masses; keep it understated. Exactly one creature, no text or labels, no borders, no new objects. Full creature remains fully within the frame.
